title: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence
summary: Given strings s and t of lowercase English letters, determine the least number of characters to add to s to make t a subsequence of s.
statement: Given strings s and t of lowercase English letters, determine the least number of characters to add to s to make t a subsequence of s. A subsequence is formed by deleting characters from s without altering the order of the remaining characters.
constraints: Append characters only to the end of s.
After appending, t must be a subsequence of the resulting string.
Return the minimum number of appended characters.
hints: Greedily match the next unmatched target character while scanning s left to right.
The scan length is the longest prefix of t already present as a subsequence of s.
Only the unmatched suffix of t must be appended, in its existing order.
Greedy earliest matches leave the most source characters available for later target positions, so no other matching can cover a longer prefix.
editorial: Greedy earliest matches leave the most source characters available for later target positions, so no other matching can cover a longer prefix.

The target is already a subsequence, so no characters are appended.
